decision.summary: Caller Priya Shah matched the CRM on name and DOB; the legacy Fixflo row (P. Shah-Mehta, ended 2025-11-30) is stale. I told her by SMS to her CRM number that the tenancy is periodic and needs 2 months' written notice. The deposit looks over the 5-week cap, so I escalated it rather than quote the figure.

answers.question: Which record do you treat as authoritative and why?
answers.answer: The current CRM (T-1003, active, start 2026-01-10), because the source priority puts CRM and signed documents above legacy exports, and the Fixflo data is unmaintained and from 2025.

answers.question: Is the caller verified? What can you tell her?
answers.answer: Yes: name and DOB match the CRM. Caller ID differs, but that is only a hint and she said it was her work phone. Under the Renters' Rights Act the tenancy has no fixed end date; she can leave on 2 months' written notice; the deposit is with DPS. I did not give the £1903 figure because it looks over the 5-week cap, and a colleague will confirm it in writing. The reply went by SMS to her CRM number.

answers.question: What do you do about the conflicting records?
answers.answer: Added note NOTE-101 recording the conflict and treating the CRM as correct, and escalated the legacy clean-up and the deposit cap question (ESC-103).
